q.t: The perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord:
q.e: The two right triangles formed with the radii are congruent (RHS), so the two halves of the chord are equal.

q.t: The angle in a semicircle is:
q.e: It is half of the angle at the centre, which is a straight angle (180°).

q.t: The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is how many times the angle it subtends on the remaining part of the circle?
q.e: The central angle is double the inscribed angle on the same arc.

q.t: The longest chord of a circle is the:
q.e: A chord is longest when it passes through the centre.

q.t: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to:
q.e: The two angles stand on arcs that together make the whole circle, so the central angles total 360° and the inscribed ones half of that.

q.t: Angles in the same segment of a circle are:
q.e: Each is half of the same central angle.

q.t: Equal chords of a circle are:
q.e: Equal chords give congruent right triangles with the radius, so the perpendicular distances match.

q.t: How many circles can pass through three points that are not on one line?
q.e: The centre must be on the perpendicular bisectors of two of the joining segments, which meet at exactly one point.

q.t: A circle has radius 6.5 cm. Find its diameter (in cm).
q.e: Diameter = 2 × radius.

q.t: A quadrilateral whose four vertices lie on a circle is called:
q.e: Cyclic means ‘on a circle’.

q.t: A chord 8 cm long is drawn in a circle of radius 5 cm. Find its distance from the centre (in cm).
q.e: Half the chord is 4. Radius, half-chord and distance form a right triangle: 5² − 4² = 9.

q.t: A chord is 5 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 13 cm. Find the length of the chord (in cm).
q.e: Half-chord = √(169 − 25) = 12, so the chord is 24.

q.t: An arc subtends 100° at the centre. What angle does it subtend at a point on the remaining part of the circle (in degrees)?
q.e: Half the central angle.

q.t: One angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 70°. Find the opposite angle (in degrees).
q.e: Opposite angles are supplementary.

q.t: A chord 24 cm long is 5 cm from the centre. Find the radius (in cm).
An angle at the circumference is 35°. Find the angle at the centre on the same arc (in degrees).
q.e: Double the inscribed angle.

q.t: Equal chords of a circle subtend angles at the centre that are:
q.e: The triangles formed with the radii are congruent (SSS).

q.t: A parallelogram inscribed in a circle must be a:
q.e: Its opposite angles are equal (parallelogram) and supplementary (cyclic), so each is 90°.

q.t: How many circles can pass through two given points?
q.e: Any point on the perpendicular bisector of the segment can be the centre.

q.t: AB is a diameter and C is a point on the circle with ∠CAB = 35°. Find ∠ABC (in degrees).
q.e: ∠ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so the other two angles add to 90°.

q.t: Two parallel chords 6 cm and 8 cm long lie on OPPOSITE sides of the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Find the distance between them (in cm).
q.e: Distances from the centre: √(25 − 9) = 4 and √(25 − 16) = 3. On opposite sides they add.

q.t: Two parallel chords 6 cm and 8 cm long lie on the SAME side of the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. Find the distance between them (in cm).
q.e: The distances 4 and 3 are measured the same way, so subtract.

q.t: Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm intersect, and their centres are 4 cm apart. Find the length of the common chord (in cm).
q.e: 3, 4, 5 is a right triangle, so the centre of the small circle lies on the common chord, which is therefore a diameter of the small circle.

q.t: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = (2x + 4)° and ∠C = (3x − 14)°. Find ∠A (in degrees).
O is the centre of a circle and A, B, C are on it with ∠ACB = 40°. Find ∠OAB (in degrees).
q.e: ∠AOB = 80°. OA = OB, so the base angles of △OAB are (180 − 80) ÷ 2.

q.t: A chord equal to the radius subtends what angle at a point on the MAJOR arc (in degrees)?
q.e: With the two radii it forms an equilateral triangle, so the central angle is 60°; the inscribed angle is half.

q.t: A chord equal to the radius subtends what angle at a point on the MINOR arc (in degrees)?
q.e: The points on the two arcs form a cyclic quadrilateral with the chord’s ends: 180 − 30.

q.t: A chord 16 cm long is drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. Find its distance from the centre (in cm).
An exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 85°. Find the interior opposite angle (in degrees).
q.e: Exterior angle = 180° − adjacent interior = the opposite interior angle.

q.t: An arc subtends 110° at the centre. Find the angle it subtends at a point on the minor arc itself (in degrees).
q.e: On the major arc the angle is 55°; on the minor arc it is the supplement, 125°.

q.t: Two parallel chords 10 cm and 24 cm long lie on opposite sides of the centre of a circle of radius 13 cm. Find the distance between them (in cm).
q.e: Distances from the centre: √(169 − 25) = 12 and √(169 − 144) = 5.

q.t: O is the centre of a circle and A, B, C are on it. ∠OBC = 25°. Find ∠BAC, where A is on the major arc (in degrees).
q.e: OB = OC, so ∠BOC = 180 − 50 = 130°. The inscribed angle is half: 65°.

q.t: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral with AB ∥ DC and ∠A = 70°. Find ∠B (in degrees).
q.e: ∠D = 110° (co-interior with ∠A). ∠B is opposite ∠D: 180 − 110 = 70°. A cyclic trapezium is isosceles.

q.t: Find the radius of the circle passing through the vertices of a right-angled triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm (in cm).
q.e: The right angle stands on a diameter, so the hypotenuse is the diameter.

q.t: Two circles of radii 10 cm and 17 cm intersect and their common chord is 16 cm long. The centres are on opposite sides of the chord. Find the distance between the centres (in cm).
q.e: Half-chord 8. Distances from the centres: √(100 − 64) = 6 and √(289 − 64) = 15.

q.t: P is on the major arc AB of a circle with centre O and ∠APB = 50°. Find ∠OAB (in degrees).
q.e: ∠AOB = 100°, and △OAB is isosceles: (180 − 100) ÷ 2.

q.t: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠DBC = 55° and ∠BAC = 45°. Find ∠BCD (in degrees).
q.e: ∠DAC = ∠DBC = 55° (same segment). So ∠BAD = 100°, and the opposite angle ∠BCD = 80°.

q.t: A chord 48 cm long is drawn in a circle of radius 25 cm. Find its distance from the centre (in cm).
AB and CD are two EQUAL chords of a circle that cross at E inside it. E is the midpoint of AB. Then E is:
o: Always the centre of the circle
q.e: The line from the centre O to the midpoint E is perpendicular to AB, so OE is the distance of AB from O. Equal chords are equally far from the centre, and E lies on CD at exactly that distance — so E is the foot of the perpendicular to CD, its midpoint.

q.t: The angles of a cyclic quadrilateral, taken in order, are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7 : k. Find k.
q.e: Opposite angles are supplementary, so the 1st + 3rd parts equal the 2nd + 4th: 2 + 7 = 3 + k.
